$comment: Root ADR-0336: the one registry of the schemas Foundation publishes to users and downstream. A subject is one kind of published document; its revisions are append-only (a merged revision and its schema file never change, scripts/guard/schema-registry.sh) and each one is held to the subject's compatibility mode against every earlier revision of its major (scripts/schema_registry.py check). A document names its subject and major in `schema_version` (`<subject>.v<major>`), and from the first revision registered here on its revision in `schema_revision`; consumers check the subject and the major only. A revision marked `legacy` was served before the registry and keeps the string it was served under, a frozen alias of its major: no new revision may be legacy, and no later major may take a number a legacy string already holds. `consumers` is each reader's pact: the paths it reads, a `required` one being a path it cannot do without, which every revision of the subject's major must guarantee. `record` names the pre-registry field record a legacy revision was translated from (contracts/by-pnu-documents), held equal to it. The subjects not listed here keep their earlier mechanism (config/r2-connections.contract.json document_schema_version, contracts/by-pnu-documents) until they are moved one at a time.

revisions.reason: the first served document: a parcel's open onbid rounds, the Gold JSON column as written
each round gains its media index (rounds[].photos[], content-addressed by sha256), an optional field: an expansion of revision 1 served under its own string before the registry existed

every collected Onbid field a buyer reads, all optional: each round gains the rest of its list row (the provider's code names, bid conditions, organisations); the document gains items[] (detail with the 공매재산명세서, tenancy, occupancy, rights, areas, corrections and appraisals; bid information with earlier rounds and every round's schedule; closed rounds' results; maps) and announcements[] (text, attachments, organisation, opening), once each for the rounds that name them
